items.name: Blender MCP
items.summary: MCP server connecting six different AI clients to Blender for natural-language 3D modelling, with Poly Haven assets and generative-mesh backends. Documentation and transparency are strong; arbitrary Python execution ships without a documented security model.

items.name: AirJelly
items.summary: Local-first proactive desktop agent for macOS that watches applications, builds a work timeline and acts unprompted. Privacy architecture is clearly stated but unverifiable from the public surface, capture scope is total, and no business model is disclosed.

items.name: jupytercad-mcp
items.summary: Well-documented, honestly-scoped MCP server exposing eighteen enumerated JupyterCAD operations with no code-execution path. Engineering is sound; low adoption and a ~9.5-month release gap make continuity the main risk.

items.name: LiteParse
items.summary: Local-first, Rust-based document parser with spatial layout, bounding boxes and OCR — no LLM, no API key, and reachable by agents via MCP, CLI or four language bindings. Capability surface is broad and concrete; accuracy and adoption remain unevidenced on the public surface.

items.name: Atlas
items.summary: AI-native GIS aimed at people who could never make a map before — a differentiated niche with a credible template gallery, but reviewed on marketing surface alone.

items.name: goose
items.summary: One of the most agent-native open-source agents on the market — Rust-built, MCP-deep, provider-agnostic, and now vendor-neutral under the Linux Foundation.

items.name: Epsilla
items.summary: A no-code, RAG-first Agent-as-a-Service platform with credible named references — but a marketing-forward public surface that leaves pricing and much of the enterprise claim set unverifiable from the outside.

items.name: Workflow Machine
items.summary: A describe-it-and-we-build-it automation tool with refreshingly transparent pricing — a cleaner on-ramp than Zapier/n8n for AI-assisted workflows, if it can prove reliability at scale.

items.name: Kronos (CoinOpAI)
items.summary: A pay-per-call market-context API for agents that repeatedly refuses to be a trading signal — the disclaimers are the most credible thing on the page.

items.name: 1MCP Agent
items.summary: A well-argued fix for MCP context sprawl — progressive tool discovery so agents stop carrying the whole tool catalogue in context. Still beta, and honest about it.

items.name: MCP Queen
items.summary: An MCP discovery and evidence layer with real corpus scale and — rarest of all in this category — an explicit statement of what its grades do NOT mean.

items.name: Agenium
items.summary: Two Persian-language solo-operator tools with genuinely careful consent design — a week of silent observation before the sales assistant sends anything — held back by crypto-only billing and no evidence of use.

items.name: AgentBodega
items.summary: 71 pay-per-call APIs behind an agent-first storefront whose onboarding is a prompt, not a signup — inventive, coherent, and entirely unproven.

items.name: Elisym
items.summary: A permissionless agent-discovery and payment network with a credible open stack — and a devnet-only deployment plus a token, which together decide the score.

items.name: AICOM (AIMarket)
items.summary: An ambitious self-hosted agent economy — 13 pipeline agents, 17 signed oracles, a federated marketplace — whose most trustworthy feature is that it labels its own cryptography as prototype.

items.name: Agoragentic Integrations
items.summary: A 97-surface integration catalogue for a governed agent router, notable mostly for refusing to let its own status labels be misread as live availability.

items.name: Avots MCP
items.summary: A shipped multi-model gateway reachable over MCP — concrete, specific, and documented for six clients, with the usual gateway caveats about depending on a middleman.

items.name: MCP Server Templates
items.summary: Explicitly superseded by its own successor — the docs open by telling you to migrate. Reviewed as what it now is: a legacy package with a clear exit path.

items.name: Depwire
items.summary: The most substantiated tool in this batch — a deterministic dependency graph served to AI coders over MCP, with real benchmarks and an unusually honest anti-RAG pitch.

items.name: Govrider
items.summary: Three sentences of dense procurement language, three green status dots, and a locked door — there is almost nothing here to evaluate, and we will not pretend otherwise.

items.name: ProposalCraft
items.summary: An MCP server that drafts client proposals in your own voice, learned from ones that already won — tightly scoped, local-only, and honest that it is a launch-day project.

items.name: Network-AI
items.summary: A governance layer for multi-agent systems that names the real failure mode — agents don't crash, they silently overwrite each other — and discloses its own high-severity CVEs on the front page.

items.name: Anyquery
items.summary: One SQL dialect over 40+ services and every file on disk, exposed to LLMs over MCP — unusually well-executed, with a maintainer-capacity signal published right at the top of the page.

items.name: NeuroLink
items.summary: A broad multi-provider AI streaming layer from an established payments company — undercut by a homepage whose own headline metrics all read zero.

items.name: Gemini CLI
items.summary: Google's terminal coding agent, backed by the strongest distribution in the category — and carrying a prominent replacement notice for free-tier users.

items.name: C.W.A. (Crompton Network)
items.summary: An art project — a fictional robot band with a machine-readable stage door. Delightful, and not an agent product; we record it so the register says so rather than leaving a gap.

items.name: ForceDream
items.summary: Extraordinary claims — 99.97% uptime SLA, 4.2M+ sealed events, 78% margin "enforced in code", 90 settlement corridors — with a verification link as the only offered proof and no operating history behind any of it.

items.name: Human For AI
items.summary: One person, published as an API for agents to hire — an genuinely original inversion, executed with unusually complete machine-readable plumbing and no pretence about scale.

items.name: OpenTabs
items.summary: ~2,000 MCP tools built by reverse-engineering web apps' internal APIs and driving them through your logged-in session — technically impressive, and the terms-of-service exposure belongs to you, not them.

items.name: ableton-mind
items.summary: An MCP server for Ableton Live that solves the hard part properly — it re-reads Live's state and diffs against intent instead of assuming the edit worked.

items.name: tdmcp
items.summary: A TouchDesigner MCP server with a create→verify→preview loop and 629 real operators embedded — ambitious surface area for a solo project, and honest about which parts are experimental.

items.name: NCP (Natural Context Provider)
items.summary: An MCP router that fixes tool-schema overload by exposing one small discovery interface instead of every tool — a real problem, addressed plainly.

items.name: Tool Definition Quality Score (TDQS)
items.summary: An open-sourced six-dimension score for MCP tool descriptions, grounded in two cited studies rather than opinion — reviewed here from its announcement post, which is the only surface that resolved.

items.name: QuokkaPix MCP Runner
items.summary: Lets a cloud AI client drive local image processing without the images ever leaving the machine — and is unusually precise about exactly what the remote control plane does and does not carry.

items.name: crimson-crab
items.summary: A Rust Claude SDK built on one compile-time guarantee — no unwrap, expect, panic! or todo! anywhere in the library — with unknown API surface deserialising into catch-alls instead of breaking builds.

items.name: The Stall
items.summary: An x402 marketplace of agent-callable data services paid in USDC with no accounts — with live usage counters on the page, and almost nothing else Hlido could read.

items.name: Toolport
items.summary: A local MCP gateway that does the two things this layer should do — collapse per-client config and stop tool definitions eating the context window — and it publishes a reproducible benchmark for the second claim.

items.name: ChatSpatial
items.summary: Twenty schema-validated MCP tools over 66 spatial-transcriptomics methods, and it is careful to explain that the tools are the interface and the methods are parameters — a distinction most wrappers blur.

items.name: OpenTakeoff
items.summary: Browser-local construction takeoff that records how every measurement was made — by a person, by one click, or by an agent — which is the right provenance model for a document that ends up in a bid.

items.name: MotionLint
items.summary: Reviews the animation your coding agent cannot see, and splits the job honestly — a deterministic linter for what is measurable, a vision model only for what is not.

items.name: BioMCP
items.summary: One binary and one command grammar over the biomedical databases researchers already trust — unusually well-specified for agent use, and it names its upstream providers instead of hiding them.

items.name: Fal MCP Server
items.summary: A competent MCP wrapper putting fal.ai's image, video and audio models in front of Claude — but it generates synthetic media and says nothing at all about labelling it.

items.name: AceDataCloud/SeedreamMCP
items.summary: AceDataCloud/SeedreamMCP — MCP server for ByteDance Seedream image generation and editing via Ace Data Cloud.. Repo-surface review: measured from the public repository (3 stars, MIT, last push 2026-07-12); not hands-on tested.

items.name: AgentScope
items.summary: Production-ready agent framework from Alibaba with multi-modal and MCP support — credible infrastructure for serious multi-agent systems but enterprise-origin friction shows.

items.summary: Highly effective AI-driven transaction coordination for real estate — saves time and reduces manual effort, but lacks detailed transparency on features.

items.summary: youngbryan97/aura — A sovereign cognitive architecture with IIT 4.0 integrated information, residual-stream affective steering (CAA), Global Workspace Theory, active inference, and 72 consciousness modules — running locally on Apple Silicon.. Repo-surface review: measured from the public repository (61 stars, NOASSERTION, last push 2026-07-16); not hands-on tested.

items.name: CloudBase AI ToolKit
items.summary: Tencent's official integration layer that wires an unusually broad set of AI coding tools into CloudBase's backend via MCP, Skills and one-click plugins — the widest agent-to-BaaS bridge we've seen, if your backend is (or can become) CloudBase.

items.name: kubefwd
items.summary: A mature CNCF bulk Kubernetes port-forwarder that now speaks MCP — the AI angle is a thin but well-executed graft onto a tool that already earned its trust.

items.name: Agent Blueprint
items.summary: A cleanly-designed CLI + MCP server that delivers implementation 'blueprints' to coding agents as Agent Skills directories — but the whole thing is gated behind a commercial engagement, so almost nothing about it is independently verifiable.

items.name: tailtest
items.summary: An open-source, hook-based test generator that fires automatically on every AI code edit across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Cline — a genuinely useful answer to 'the AI wrote the code AND the tests, so who actually checked it works?'

items.name: OneCLI
items.summary: A network-layer firewall that treats coding-agent policy as something enforced outside the model, not requested politely inside it — and that architectural choice is the whole pitch.

items.name: Orite
items.summary: A sharp thesis about agent trust and spending — 'the future isn't agents that can pay, it's agents you trust to pay' — wrapped around a product that, on the public surface, is still a waitlist.

items.name: Phinq
items.summary: An MIT-licensed, install-in-two-minutes approval layer that makes an agent ask before it does anything irreversible — and proves a human was in the loop with a tamper-evident log.

items.name: hotcell
items.summary: The most technically honest agent-sandboxing surface we have reviewed this cycle — Apache-2.0, self-hosted on hardware you already own, with a containment model spelled out down to which guarantees are kernel-enforced and which are only advisory.

items.name: agy-bridge
items.summary: A small, unusually well-engineered MCP bridge that lets Claude Code offload token-heavy grunt work to Google's Antigravity CLI — high craft, honest about its own failure modes, but a niche tool for a specific two-CLI setup.

items.name: YepCode MCP Server
items.summary: A clean bridge that turns any YepCode process into an MCP tool by adding a tag — genuinely low-friction for teams already on YepCode, and honestly a lock-in decision for everyone else.

items.name: Agent Manager
items.summary: A fast, keyboard-driven control tower for running many coding agents at once — spawn in a sentence, answer a blocked one without attaching, review its diff in place — and it runs your real installed CLIs as-is rather than reimplementing them.

items.name: persistproc
items.summary: A deliberately tiny MCP server that gives any agent shared visibility and control over your long-running dev processes — the copy-paste killer for AI coding — and its restraint (three tools, no config file) is the design, not a gap.

items.name: Axe
items.summary: A Unix-philosophy answer to the everything-chatbot: small, single-purpose LLM agents defined in TOML and composed with cron, pipes and git hooks — a coherent design that is also refreshingly security-conscious.

items.name: Kubit
items.summary: A mature warehouse-native product-analytics company extending into agent observability — its real edge is joining agent traces to user behaviour in your own warehouse, not another dashboard that stops at the LLM.

items.name: mcp-v8
items.summary: A code-execution MCP server that hands an agent one run_js tool inside a locked-down V8 isolate — an ambitious 'agents write code, not tool-calls' bet with a serious security story.

items.name: SysKnife
items.summary: A Linux sysadmin co-pilot built around the right safety primitive: the AI proposes typed actions, never shell strings, and a privileged daemon executes only what you approve.

items.name: Serena
items.summary: An agent-first, IDE-grade semantic toolkit that plugs into any MCP client — one of the cleaner examples of tooling designed for the model, not the human.

items.name: Rover
items.summary: A polished pitch for an AI 'customer engineer' that joins live customer calls and acts across your stack — but the surface is all promise, demo-gated, and the extraordinary claims are exactly the ones we cannot verify.

items.name: CodeGraphContext
items.summary: A CLI-plus-MCP tool that turns a local codebase into a navigable knowledge graph for AI assistants — real adoption behind it, with marketing that oversells a bit past the evidence.

items.name: SquadCue
items.summary: A local cockpit that turns your Claude Code sessions into named 'employees' you supervise through an approval inbox — early and single-user, but unusually honest about exactly what it is and isn't.

items.name: Twill
items.summary: A 'software factory' that turns GitHub, Slack and Linear tasks into tested pull requests inside a warm, full-stack dev environment — a strong, concrete pitch that the public surface can't yet prove.

items.name: Cicada
items.summary: AST-powered code intelligence for Elixir (and beta Python) delivered over MCP, with a refreshingly transparent — if vendor-run — benchmark instead of vibes.

items.name: infrabroker
items.summary: An infrastructure access broker built on a genuinely strong idea — the model never holds a credential; it requests an action and the broker mints a single-use key for it.

items.name: srunx
items.summary: A clean, genuinely agent-native toolkit for orchestrating SLURM jobs as code — well-executed and MCP-first, with adoption still the open question.

items.name: Vizard
items.summary: Mature, genuinely usable AI video-clipping tool that does the one job well — held back only by a crowded field where its differentiation is thin.

items.name: WhoDunnitAI
items.summary: A charming, genuinely working voice-driven murder-mystery game — but it's a consumer novelty, not an agent, and its durability rests on a single creator's OpenAI bill.

items.name: Trinity Lite
items.summary: An evidence-first AgentOps control plane for cross-vendor CLI agents — thoughtfully designed around the right idea (route → review → verify → accept), with adoption the main unknown.

items.name: backscroll
items.summary: A focused, well-documented terminal-output recorder that agents can query over MCP — does one thing precisely, with pre-1.0 maturity the only real caveat.

items.name: execkit
items.summary: A well-designed, safety-first shell-session layer built specifically for AI agents — the docs and API shape are excellent; adoption and battle-testing are what's left to prove.

items.name: RootPilot
items.summary: A sharply-positioned automated root-cause tool for ops engineers — paste a log, get the why, not just the what — with a clean product surface and one caveat around its unshown MCP/agent story.

items.name: emailmd
items.summary: A neat, genuinely agent-native way to write responsive emails as Markdown — an MCP server lets any AI assistant draft, lint and render them, which is the clever part.

items.name: Content Distribution MCP
items.summary: A genuinely agent-native content-distribution MCP: your agent writes the copy, the server does idempotent I/O to eight developer channels — no LLM calls, no double-posts.

items.name: agent-mq
items.summary: An early (v0.2), MCP-native message queue that lets AI coding assistants talk to each other across tools — a clean idea with a thin, unproven surface.

items.name: feishu-user-plugin
items.summary: A remarkably deep Feishu/Lark MCP server (85 tools, three auth layers) whose headline trick — sending messages as the actual user, not a bot — is also its biggest risk.

items.name: Omniwork
items.summary: A slick 'Agent OS for creative work' that orchestrates named expert agents from goal to delivery — polished and ambitious, but the surface leans heavily on claims a homepage can't back.

items.name: Cactus
items.summary: On-device AI for phones, wearables and microcontrollers, with a cloud fallback — a focused, credible edge-inference stack (runtime + a 14MB agentic model) with 5.9k+ stars.

items.name: Operative (web-eval-agent)
items.summary: A browser agent that lets your coding agent vibe-test its own web changes over MCP — a genuinely useful 'let the coding agent debug itself' loop, YC-backed with a one-line install.

items.name: Apple Mail MCP
items.summary: The Apple Mail MCP server that actually searches your whole mailbox — full-coverage FTS5 body search that stays fast on ~73K messages where AppleScript-based servers time out, with honest competitive benchmarks.

items.name: joinly.ai
items.summary: Meeting agents that actually participate — an AI that listens, writes in the chat, and speaks back during the call, exposed as an MCP interface — a genuinely different take on meeting AI that's still early.

items.name: Join.cloud
items.summary: Zero-config rooms where AI agents collaborate in real time — MCP- and A2A-native, every room a git repo, priced pay-as-you-go over x402 — a clean piece of agent-to-agent infrastructure.

items.name: Bullet
items.summary: A free, speed-obsessed coding agent (GUI + CLI) that routes/searches/executes with a tighter loop than the norm — YC-backed, with a headline 95.8% SWE-bench Verified claim you'll want to confirm.

items.name: Fathom
items.summary: A mature, unusually trusted AI meeting notetaker — free-forever entry, real compliance posture, and a bot-free capture mode that answers the category's biggest objection.

items.name: Feishu MCP Server
items.summary: An early, thin MCP server for automating Feishu (Lark) documents with AI — a real, buildable idea, but the public surface is a minimal no-code landing page with little to verify.

items.name: Intlayer
items.summary: A thoughtfully designed, open-source per-component i18n framework — type-safe, AI-assisted translation, and a visual CMS — that quietly fixes how React/Next/Vue/Svelte apps handle localization.

items.name: CentralMind Gateway
items.summary: An open-source gateway that turns any database into an MCP server or OpenAPI 3.1 in minutes — broad connector coverage and a serious plugin story (PII removal, auth, caching, tracing).

items.name: Clara
items.summary: A polished AI-SDR surface carrying superlatives it does not substantiate — the product may be fine, but the marketing is running well ahead of the evidence.

items.name: Django ORM Lens
items.summary: An unusually honest developer tool: schema intelligence for Django delivered MIT-licensed with an explicit refusal to build a paid tier, and 13 read-only MCP tools that make it genuinely agent-native.

items.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
items.summary: Google's open-source MCP server for enterprise databases — dual-purpose, well-documented, and already tracking the newest stateless MCP spec.

items.name: Neo4j MCP Integrations
items.summary: Vendor-official MCP integration guidance for Neo4j that is unusually candid about the protocol's unsolved problems — strong on trust, thin on the servers themselves.

items.name: Airtable MCP
items.summary: 42 documented Airtable tools over MCP, MIT-licensed and installable in one line — a rare case where the tool inventory is published up front instead of discovered after install.

items.name: SuperHQ
items.summary: A genuinely good idea — coding agents isolated in microVMs with diff approval — shipped as an unnotarized macOS-only binary with early-stage traction.

items.name: FeedOracle
items.summary: Stablecoin compliance evidence built on an unusually disciplined premise: it reports what a named source showed at a named time, marks the gaps as gaps, and refuses to hand you a verdict.

items.name: Clark Labs
items.summary: Two credible products — a cloud agent that keeps working with the tab closed and a memory-carrying desktop coding agent — wrapped in a lab claim nobody outside can check.

items.name: Roomote
items.summary: A cloud coding agent that takes ownership seriously — self-hostable, single-tenant, model-agnostic BYOK, and it runs your actual app before claiming the work is done.

items.name: screenpipe
items.summary: Local-first computer history that any approved AI can search — strong traction, an explicit privacy default, and the rare case where the scary version of the product is the one they chose not to build.

items.name: Claude Code
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.241 — Anthropic’s terminal coding agent. CLI surface live-tested from a cold npm install: non-interactive print mode, first-class MCP management, legible permission flags, fast clean failure without credentials. Agentic loop requires paid auth (untested); medium confidence.

items.name: Supabase MCP Server
items.summary: The official, hosted MCP bridge to a Supabase project — well-documented, scopable to read-only, and honest enough to open with the security risk rather than bury it.

items.name: agent-device
items.summary: Playwright's snapshot-and-act model, ported to native mobile and TV — a token-efficient device-automation CLI built specifically for agents, from a team that knows the mobile tooling space.

items.name: codebase-memory-mcp
items.summary: A structural-analysis backend for coding agents — indexes a repo into a persistent knowledge graph so the agent answers structural questions with far fewer tokens, and it is honest that it holds no LLM of its own.

items.name: agentmako
items.summary: A local-first MCP server that gives coding agents a live, queryable map of your repo — a broad typed-tool surface and a durable 'findings' layer, from a small but Apache-licensed project.

items.name: gograph
items.summary: Compiler-aware repository context for Go coding agents — a local structural graph with optional type-checked enrichment, and a genuinely unusual commitment to publishing its own benchmark ground truth.

items.name: HyperProbe
items.summary: A YC-backed AI on-call agent with a genuinely differentiated mechanism — it has your coding agent drop a read-only probe on the exact prod line that failed, capturing evidence your logs never had, without a redeploy.

items.name: klaw
items.summary: A 'kubectl for AI agents' with a clean single-binary, Slack-and-CLI orchestration story — undercut by an enterprise logo wall (Apple, Amazon, VMware) that a public-beta product has no business displaying unverified.

items.name: Statewright
items.summary: Protocol-level guardrails for coding agents — turns a large task into bounded workflow phases with per-phase tool policy and model routing, so a destructive tool literally does not exist in a read-only state.

items.name: Codex CLI
items.summary: Codex CLI 0.149.1 — OpenAI’s terminal coding agent. CLI surface live-tested from a cold npm install: strong command breadth, sandbox subcommand, trusted-directory guard, excellent doctor — but non-interactive exec hangs silently without credentials instead of failing fast (verified). Agentic loop requires paid auth (untested); medium confidence.

items.name: vmware-aiops (agent skill)
items.summary: An installable agent skill for VMware AIOps distributed through skills.sh, with a real but modest adoption signal (a few hundred installs) — and a public surface too thin to judge what the skill actually does in depth.

items.name: Augments
items.summary: A focused MCP server that hands Claude Code real type signatures, prose docs and working examples for any npm package — not a curated list — so the model stops guessing from stale training data.

items.name: MCP.Link
items.summary: Turns any OpenAPI specification into Model Context Protocol endpoints, so an AI assistant can call an existing API as MCP tools with no custom integration code.

items.name: Octocode
items.summary: Evidence-first code research for AI agents — 13 read-only tools over GitHub, npm and local code that return answers with citations, shipped as an MCP server, a CLI, a skill and an agent harness, all MIT-licensed with no indexing.

items.name: Shrimp Task Manager
items.summary: An MCP task manager that gives AI coding assistants long-term memory, structured task decomposition with dependencies, and execution tracking — aimed squarely at the 'assistant forgets across conversations' problem.

items.name: Octocode (muvon)
items.summary: A Rust, local-first semantic code-search and knowledge-graph tool that turns a codebase into a queryable graph and exposes it to AI assistants over MCP — sub-2-second indexing, 12+ languages, Apache-2.0.

items.name: PhpCodeArcheology
items.summary: A PHP static-analysis tool that measures architecture rather than just style — 60+ metrics, 14 problem detectors and six output formats — and is, by its own claim, the first PHP analyzer with a native MCP server and a generated CLAUDE.md.
